analyses.name: Apple Inc.
analyses.verdict: A confirmed Stage 2 uptrend carrying an RSI of 37.6 - the most un-extended large-cap setup on the entire 446-name scan, and the best risk-to-reward available at this open.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended September 2025)
financials.summary: Apple is now two businesses wearing one badge. The hardware franchise - iPhone, Mac, iPad, Wearables - is a replacement-cycle business whose unit volumes are broadly mature and whose growth comes from mix and pricing rather than new customers. Sitting on top of it is the Services layer: the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music and TV, advertising, payments, and the search-placement economics with Google. Services carries roughly double the gross margin of hardware, and because it grows off the installed base rather than off new device sales, it converts Apple's two-billion-plus active devices into an annuity. That mix shift is the single most important line in the financial statements: revenue growth of 16.4% year over year paired with EPS growth of 28.7% is only possible when the faster-growing half of the business is also the higher-margin half, and the gap between those two numbers is the operating leverage the market is paying 33.2x forward earnings for. The balance sheet remains the strongest at this scale in the market - the company generates far more operating cash than it can reinvest, which is why the buyback is structural rather than opportunistic and why share count reduction adds a percentage point or two to EPS growth every year on its own. The thing to watch in the statements is not the revenue line but the services gross margin and the capital-return pace, because those two together explain most of the EPS number.
highlights: Revenue +16.4% year over year - a genuine reacceleration for a company of this size
EPS +28.7% year over year, running well ahead of revenue - the Services mix shift and buyback compounding together
Services is the margin engine: roughly double hardware gross margin, growing off the installed base rather than unit sales
Forward P/E approximately 33.2x - a premium multiple that requires the Services mix to keep improving
Market capitalisation of approximately $4.62 trillion - the largest weight in the market
Buyback structurally reduces share count each year, adding to EPS growth independent of operations

accomplishments: Sustained a double-digit revenue reacceleration at $4.6 trillion of market value, which almost no company at scale manages
Grew earnings roughly twice as fast as revenue by shifting mix toward Services
Maintained the installed base as the moat: switching costs across devices, iCloud, Messages and payments keep the annuity intact
Continued the largest sustained capital-return programme in public markets, compounding per-share results

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: The highest-scoring name on the scan - a new 52-week high with the relative-strength line also at new highs and 47.7% revenue growth behind it, the rarest full-stack confirmation available.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Lilly is the clearest example in large-cap pharma of a single therapeutic franchise rewriting an entire income statement. The incretin platform - the GLP-1 and dual-agonist family addressing type 2 diabetes and obesity - has moved from a promising pipeline to the dominant revenue driver, and revenue growth of 47.7% year over year is what that transition looks like when manufacturing capacity finally catches up to demand. The critical detail in the statements is the gap between revenue growth of 47.7% and EPS growth of 26.2%: earnings are growing at roughly half the rate of the top line, and that is deliberate. Lilly has been spending enormous sums on manufacturing capacity expansion, on the clinical programmes extending the franchise into adjacent indications, and on the commercial infrastructure required to serve a patient population an order of magnitude larger than traditional specialty pharma. Those costs hit the current income statement while the revenue they unlock arrives over the following years. That is why the forward multiple of 27.1x is lower than a 47%-growth business would normally command - the market is discounting both the reinvestment drag and the eventual competitive response. The balance sheet comfortably funds the buildout from operating cash flow. The number that matters most going forward is gross margin on the incretin franchise as capacity utilisation improves, because that is where the reinvestment drag reverses into operating leverage.
highlights: Revenue +47.7% year over year - the fastest top-line growth of any mega-cap on this scan
EPS +26.2% - growing strongly but at roughly half the revenue rate, reflecting heavy capacity and clinical reinvestment
Forward P/E approximately 27.1x - undemanding relative to the growth rate, which reflects competitive and reinvestment discounting
Market capitalisation of approximately $1.14 trillion
The incretin franchise dominates the revenue mix; manufacturing capacity, not demand, has been the binding constraint
Reinvestment is funded from operating cash flow rather than external financing

accomplishments: Built the dominant commercial position in the largest new pharmaceutical category in decades
Executed a manufacturing scale-up that converted a supply-constrained product into a genuine revenue engine
Extended the platform into adjacent indications, widening the addressable population well beyond the original approval
Grew revenue 47.7% while remaining self-funding - the growth has not required balance-sheet leverage

analyses.name: Illumina, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A new 52-week high printed at an RSI of 49.9 - the single rarest technical combination on the 446-name scan - on a business only now emerging from a genuinely difficult three years.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Illumina is a razor-and-blade business in the middle of a repair job. It sells DNA sequencing instruments and then earns the majority of its revenue, and nearly all of its margin, on the consumables and services those instruments consume for the rest of their working lives. That installed-base annuity is what makes the company structurally attractive and also what makes it slow to turn: when academic and pharmaceutical customers defer instrument purchases, the consumables base stops growing years before it starts shrinking, and the recovery works the same way in reverse. Revenue growth of 9.4% represents a return to expansion after a stretch of decline, driven by migration of the installed base onto the higher-throughput NovaSeq X platform, where per-run consumable pull-through is materially better than on the prior generation. EPS growth remains negative at -9.4%, and the gap between recovering revenue and still-falling earnings is the entire investment question. It reflects the cost of running two instrument generations in parallel, restructuring charges, and the residual drag from the GRAIL separation that consumed management attention and capital for years. Cash generation from the consumables annuity funds the transition without external financing. What a 33.6x forward multiple pays for is not this year's earnings - it is the assumption that recurring consumables reaccelerate on a modernised installed base while the parallel-generation costs roll off, which would move earnings considerably faster than revenue.
highlights: Revenue +9.4% year over year - a return to growth after a multi-year contraction
EPS growth still NEGATIVE at -9.4%, reflecting dual-platform transition costs and restructuring

Majority of revenue is recurring consumables and services tied to the installed instrument base
NovaSeq X migration raises per-instrument consumable pull-through, the key operating lever

accomplishments: Returned the top line to growth after a multi-year contraction - the hardest part of any turnaround
Advanced the installed-base migration onto NovaSeq X, structurally raising consumable pull-through per instrument
Completed the GRAIL separation, removing a persistent capital and management-attention drain
Held the recurring consumables annuity intact through the downturn, which is what made the recovery possible

analyses.name: Elevance Health, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The cheapest name on this list at 13.4x forward earnings, sitting 0.8% above its 50-day - the tightest risk-defined entry available on any A-grade setup, and the one healthcare name that did not chase yesterday's sector melt-up.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Elevance is a managed-care organisation, which means its income statement is fundamentally a spread business: it collects premiums, pays medical claims, and keeps the difference less administrative cost. The single most important number is the medical loss ratio - the share of premium dollars paid out in claims - and the last fiscal year was defined by that ratio running hotter than priced. Revenue growth of 1.4% and EPS growth of -13.1% together tell the story precisely: membership and premium were roughly flat while claims costs rose, compressing the underwriting margin. The drivers have been elevated utilisation across the Medicare Advantage and Medicaid books - post-pandemic care catch-up, higher-acuity members after Medicaid redeterminations, and specialty drug costs including the same GLP-1 category that is powering Lilly's income statement. The offsetting structural asset is Carelon, the health-services and pharmacy-benefit arm, which earns fee-based rather than underwriting margin and is far less exposed to the claims cycle. Managed care is a repricing business by design: premiums reset annually, so a bad utilisation year is followed by a pricing correction, and the market's willingness to pay only 13.4x forward earnings reflects doubt about how many annual cycles that correction will take. The balance sheet and cash generation are not in question; the margin is.
highlights: Revenue +1.4% year over year - essentially flat membership and premium
EPS -13.1% year over year - the medical loss ratio ran above pricing, compressing underwriting margin
Forward P/E approximately 13.4x - by a wide margin the cheapest multiple among these eleven names
Market capitalisation of approximately $86 billion
Elevated utilisation in Medicare Advantage and Medicaid is the identified pressure point, including specialty and GLP-1 drug cost
Carelon health services provides fee-based margin that is structurally insulated from the claims cycle

accomplishments: Held membership and premium broadly stable through a difficult utilisation cycle rather than buying growth at bad prices
Continued to build Carelon as a fee-based earnings stream that diversifies away from pure underwriting risk
Maintained the capital position and cash generation while absorbing the margin compression
Repriced the book into the annual premium cycle, which is the structural mechanism by which managed care recovers

analyses.name: EOG Resources, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A new 52-week high at an RSI of only 55.0, in the best-converting sector on the board - and it did nothing in the last session while healthcare ran 5.4%. A leading group resting is a better entry than a leading group running.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: EOG is a shale exploration and production company that has spent a decade positioning itself as the low-cost operator rather than the fastest-growing one, and the last fiscal year is what that discipline produces when commodity prices cooperate. Revenue growth of 58.7% and EPS growth of 109.4% reflect the defining characteristic of E&P economics: the cost structure is largely fixed against a realised price that is entirely variable, so operating leverage on the way up is extreme. Earnings grew at nearly twice the rate of revenue for exactly that reason. The core assets are premium acreage in the Permian, Eagle Ford and Delaware basins where the company's stated return thresholds are set well above prevailing strip prices, meaning it declines wells that competitors would drill. That is why the balance sheet carries very little net debt relative to peers and why free cash flow, rather than production growth, is the metric management runs the business on. The capital-allocation policy follows from it: maintenance capital first, base dividend second, and then variable returns to shareholders from what remains. At 10.3x forward earnings the market is applying a mid-cycle commodity assumption rather than the current strip - which is the correct way to value an E&P, and also the reason these multiples never expand much even in good years.
highlights: Revenue +58.7% year over year - realised pricing plus disciplined volume
EPS +109.4% year over year, nearly double the revenue growth rate - E&P operating leverage at work
Forward P/E approximately 10.3x - the lowest multiple in this brief
Market capitalisation of approximately $78 billion
Low-cost premium acreage across the Permian, Eagle Ford and Delaware basins with return thresholds set above strip
Free-cash-flow-first capital allocation: maintenance capital, base dividend, then variable shareholder returns

accomplishments: Delivered EPS growth of 109.4% while maintaining capital discipline rather than chasing volume
Sustained a low-leverage balance sheet through a full commodity cycle, which most shale operators have not
Held to premium-return drilling thresholds, declining wells that would dilute returns
Converted commodity strength into shareholder returns rather than into production growth

analyses.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
analyses.verdict: The pullback the last session handed you - down 1.65% on rate mechanics rather than fundamentals, now 4.5% above a rising 50-day with EPS growing 46.9% at 14.3x forward earnings.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: JPMorgan is the closest thing in banking to a diversified conglomerate, and the last fiscal year demonstrated exactly why that matters. Revenue growth of 30.4% and EPS growth of 46.9% came from three engines pulling at once rather than from any single line: net interest income from the largest and cheapest deposit base in American banking; markets and investment-banking revenue, which benefits from volatility and from deal activity in ways that are uncorrelated with the lending book; and asset and wealth management, which is fee-based and largely insensitive to the rate cycle. EPS growing at roughly half again the rate of revenue reflects both operating leverage and credit costs that have stayed contained - provisioning has not consumed the revenue gains. The balance sheet carries capital ratios well above requirement, which is the reason the bank can absorb a credit cycle and keep returning capital while smaller peers retrench. The vulnerability visible right now is the same one that produced the last session's decline: net interest margin is a spread between what the bank earns on assets and pays on deposits, and a rally in bonds compresses the asset side faster than the deposit side reprices. That is a real, ongoing macro force, not a one-day event - but it is a margin question, not a solvency or credit question, and at 14.3x forward earnings the market is already applying a discount for it.
highlights: Revenue +30.4% year over year across lending, markets and fee businesses simultaneously
EPS +46.9% year over year - operating leverage plus contained credit provisioning

accomplishments: Grew revenue 30.4% while maintaining the fortress capital position that defines the franchise
Delivered EPS growth of 46.9% without releasing credit discipline to do it
Sustained leadership across investment banking, markets, consumer and wealth simultaneously - no peer covers all four
Continued capital return from a position of excess capital rather than at the expense of the balance sheet

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Freeport is a copper miner with a gold by-product, and the last fiscal year exposes exactly how that business converts price into profit. Revenue growth was NEGATIVE at -7.3% while EPS growth was +28.1% - a combination that only happens when realised pricing and cost control do the work that volume did not. Mined volumes were constrained, but the price environment and unit-cost discipline expanded the margin per pound enough to overwhelm the top-line decline. The asset base is concentrated in a small number of very large, very long-lived mines - the Grasberg complex in Indonesia and the North and South American porphyry operations - which is both the strength and the risk: these are multi-decade reserves that cannot be replicated, and they sit in jurisdictions where fiscal terms and permitting are political decisions. Copper itself is the structural story. It is the physical bottleneck in electrification, grid buildout and data-centre construction, and new supply requires roughly a decade from discovery to production, so demand growth cannot be met by a supply response on any relevant timescale. At 16.8x forward earnings the market is capitalising a mid-cycle copper price. The number that matters in the statements is unit net cash cost per pound, because that is what determines how much of any copper price move reaches the earnings line.

analyses.verdict: The best four-week relative strength of any mega-cap on the scan - RS line up 9.2% - and AI-levered through AWS without being levered to which chip vendor wins, which is exactly the distinction that mattered in the last session's semiconductor unwind.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Amazon's income statement is best read as three businesses with completely different economics stacked into one filing. The retail business - first-party sales, third-party marketplace fees and the logistics network underneath both - is enormous, low-margin and now largely built out, so incremental revenue increasingly drops through rather than requiring proportional new investment. Advertising, which sits inside the retail segment, is high-margin, fast-growing and structurally advantaged because Amazon owns purchase intent rather than inferring it. And AWS is a capital-intensive infrastructure business earning software-like operating margins that has become the primary determinant of consolidated profit. Revenue growth of 19.6% against EPS growth of 242.3% is the signature of that mix maturing all at once: the logistics buildout depreciating rather than expanding, advertising scaling on near-zero marginal cost, and AWS margin expanding on higher utilisation. That kind of EPS growth is not repeatable - it is the mathematics of operating leverage arriving in a single year off a compressed base - but the direction of the mix shift is durable. The critical variable going forward is AWS capital expenditure: the AI infrastructure buildout consumes enormous cash today for revenue that arrives over subsequent years, and how the market treats that spending determines the multiple. At 25.6x forward earnings the market is paying for AWS reacceleration, not for retail.

analyses.verdict: Sitting 0.3% above its 50-day - the tightest risk-defined entry on the entire board - at 12.9x forward earnings, with TradingView at STRONG BUY and zero sell signals. It is also a rate bet wearing equity clothing, and the fundamentals are genuinely deteriorating.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended September 2025)
financials.summary: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder in the United States by volume, and its income statement is a direct function of one variable it does not control: the mortgage rate. Revenue growth of 0.0% and EPS growth of -4.8% describe a business holding volume flat by buying it - the industry's mechanism for moving houses in a high-rate environment is the mortgage-rate buydown, where the builder pays points to lower the buyer's effective rate, and that cost lands squarely in gross margin. So flat revenue with declining earnings is the arithmetic of maintaining share through incentives. The structural strengths that make Horton the survivor in this cycle are real: it is disproportionately weighted to entry-level and first-time buyers, which is where demographic demand is deepest; it uses an option-and-land-bank model rather than owning raw land outright, which keeps the balance sheet lighter and lets it walk away from lots when the market turns; and its scale gives it purchasing advantages on materials and labour that smaller builders cannot match. Book value and the balance sheet are not the concern here - the margin is. The moment mortgage rates fall meaningfully, the incentive spend that is currently suppressing gross margin becomes unnecessary, and the earnings recovery is mechanical rather than speculative. That is the entire investment case, and it is why the market pays only 12.9x forward earnings.

analyses.name: NVIDIA Corporation
analyses.verdict: The chart is fine and the calendar is the problem - it reports in 7 days, which makes any stop meaningless because a gap goes straight through it. Own it if you already do; add after the number.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2026, ended January 2026)
financials.summary: Nvidia's financial statements are the clearest record of a genuine platform shift in computing. Revenue growth of 85.2% and EPS growth of 214.5% reflect a data-centre business that has gone from a component supplier to the sole practical vendor for large-scale AI training and, increasingly, inference. The economics are extraordinary because the moat is not only silicon: CUDA and the surrounding software stack represent well over a decade of developer investment that competitors cannot replicate by matching hardware specifications, and the systems-level products - full racks with networking, interconnect and software rather than discrete chips - raise both the average selling price and the switching cost simultaneously. That is why gross margin sits at a level normally associated with software rather than semiconductors, and why EPS grew at more than twice the rate of revenue. The critical structural question in the statements is customer concentration: an outsized share of data-centre revenue comes from a small number of hyperscalers whose capital-expenditure decisions are made annually and can be revised. The offsetting development is that those same customers are building custom silicon - which is exactly the dynamic that lifted Marvell 9.9% and knocked Broadcom 4.6% in the last session, and it is the long-run bear case in a sentence. At 16.8x forward earnings the market is applying a heavy discount for durability, not for growth.

analyses.verdict: NEW LISTING - 47 days of trading history, so read the business rather than the quant signals. Every technical level here is arbitrary because there is not enough price history to compute one.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025) - first year of public disclosure; treat all figures as early-stage public reporting
financials.summary: SpaceX's income statement is now dominated by Starlink rather than by launch. The launch business - Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy and the reusable booster fleet - is what made the company famous and is, in financial terms, the smaller and lumpier half: it is a contract business with government and commercial customers, priced per mission, with revenue recognition tied to cadence. Reusability transformed its unit economics, which is why launch has become genuinely profitable rather than a subsidised loss leader, but its growth is bounded by how many missions can physically be flown. Starlink is the other business and the one that justifies the valuation: a satellite broadband network sold on monthly subscription, which converts an enormous fixed capital outlay into recurring revenue with high incremental margin once the constellation is deployed and the customer is connected. Revenue growth of 91.9% reflects Starlink subscriber additions compounding on top of a rising launch cadence. There are effectively no earnings to speak of - the forward multiple of 84.2x tells you the market is capitalising a revenue trajectory, not a profit stream - because the capital consumption of constellation replenishment and the Starship development programme runs against current profitability. Starship is the swing factor in every direction: it is the vehicle that makes the next-generation Starlink constellation economical and the one that carries the largest execution risk on the books.

Grew Starlink into a subscription broadband business at global scale - revenue +91.9%
